''tempter.''] One who does not tempt.
{{smaller block|Sothely God is ''untempter'' of euyl thingis.
{{right|''Wyclif'', Jas. i. 13.}}}}

'''untemptible''' (un-tempt′i-bl), ''a.'' Not capable of being tempted.
{{smaller block|Absolute purity is ''untemptible'', as in God.
{{right|''Bushnell'', Sermons for New Life, xiv.}}}}

'''untemptibly''' (un-tempt′i-bli), ''adv.'' So as not to be tempted. ''Bushnell.''

'''untenability''' (un-ten-a-bil′i-ti), ''n.'' The quality or state of being untenable; indefensibleness.

'''untenable''' (un-ten′a̤-bl), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not tenable; that cannot be held in possession: as, an ''untenable'' post or fort. ''Clarendon.''—'''2.''' That cannot be maintained by argument; not defensible: as, an ''untenable'' doctrine.
{{smaller block|All others give up such false opinions as ''untenable''.
{{right|''Goldsmith'', The Bee, No. 1.}}}}

'''untenableness''' (un-ten′a̤-bl-nes), ''n.'' The character or state of being untenable; untenability.

'''untenant''' (un-ten′ant), ''v. t.'' [< ''un-''<sup>2</sup> + ''tenant''<sup>1</sup>.] To deprive of a tenant or tenants; expel or remove a dweller from; evict; dislodge.
{{smaller block|He gets possession of their affections, whence all the power of man cannot ''untenant'' him.
{{right|''Rev. T. Adams'', Works, I. 202. (''Davies.'')}}}}

'''untenantable''' (un-ten′a̤n-ta̤-bl), ''a.'' Not fit to be tenanted or occupied as a dwelling; uninhabitable.
{{smaller block|Frozen and ''untenantable'' regions. {{right|''Whewell.''}}}}

'''untenanted''' (un-ten′a̤n-ted), ''a.'' Not occupied by a tenant; not inhabited. ''Sir W. Temple.''

'''untender''' (un-ten′dėr), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not tender; not

Not inclosed in or provided with a tent or tents: as, an ''untented'' army.—'''2.''' Having no tents erected upon it: as, an ''untented'' field.—'''3.''' ''Nature'', XLIII. 554.}} '''untetchet†''', ''n.'' [ME., < ''un-'' + ''tetche'', ''tache''.] An evil habit; a disgraceful act.

readings.c3s2:
¶
'''unthinkable''' (un-thing′ka̤-bl), ''a.'' That cannot be made an object of thought; that cannot be thought; incogitable.

{{smaller block|What is contradictory is ''unthinkable.''
{{right|''Sir W. Hamilton,'' Lectures on Metaph. and Logic, III. v.}}}}

'''unthinker''' (un-thing′kėr), ''n.'' One who does not think, or who is not given to thinking; a thoughtless person. [Rare.]

{{smaller block|Thinkers and ''unthinkers'' by the million are spontaneously at their post, doing what is in them.
{{right|''Carlyle,'' French Rev., I. iv. 1. (''Davies.'')}}}}

'''unthinking''' (un-thing′king), ''a.'' '''1.''' Not thinking; heedless; without thought or care; thoughtless; inconsiderate: as, ''unthinking'' youth.

{{smaller block|It is not so easy a thing to be a brave man as the ''unthinking'' part of mankind imagine.
{{right|''Steele,'' Spectator, No. 350.}}}}

'''2.''' Not indicating thought or reflection; thoughtless.

{{smaller block|She has such a pretty ''unthinking'' Air, while she saunters round a Room, and prattles Sentences.
{{right|''Steele,'' Tender Husband, i. 1.}}}}

'''unthinkingly''' (un-thing′king-li), ''adv.'' In an unthinking manner; without reflection; thoughtlessly. ''Pope.''

'''unthinkingness''' (un-thing′king-nes), ''n.'' The character of being unthinking or thoughtless.
